newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 27.

text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Farooq Leghari said he would use his constitutional powers to dismiss the government only if it was in the supreme interest of the country.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has said the events of the past week indicated that conspiracies were being hatched against her under a time-table.
- Afghanistan's rebel Taleban Islamic militia said it had captured parts of Kabul and the main government airbase of Bagram as defending forces abandoned the besieged capital.
- Ghinwa Bhutto, wife of the slain brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has accused officials of the Sindh provincial government of conspiring to kill her husband Murtaza Bhutto.
- A team of doctors investigating the killing of Murtaza Bhutto, estranged brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, said the wound suffered by a policeman during the shootout was self-inflicted.
- Pakistani and French defence officials will meet in Paris from October 28 to discuss Pakistan's purchase of Mirage jets.
- A peaceful strike was observed in Karachi and throughout Sindh province to condemn the murder of Murtaza Bhutto and his seven companions by the police.
- Ghinwa Bhutto, has rejected the Sindh provincial government's inquiry tribunal and demanded that Supreme Court judges investigate events leading to the death of her husband.
- The price of vegetable ghee and cooking oil that rose by one rupee per kilogram on higher international price of palm oil is bound to rise after rupee devaluation on September 10.

- The Export Promotion Bureau has asked the State (central) Bank of Pakistan to arrange a meeting between the Pakistani bankers and the Iraqi Bank Rafadain to settle the account of $5.88 million owed by the Iraqi buyers to Pakistani exporters.
- Pakistan has strongly rejected Kabul regime's allegations of interference in the affairs of Afghanistan.
